# dsh-workbuddy-cny
English | 中文

> [!WARNING]
> **The default conversion rate is known to be too low (roughly half).** It was measure
d on a machine where the WorkBuddy desktop app was also consuming credits in the background, so the

denominator was inflated. See #1 for the evidence and the correction in progress.
>
> The plugin its
elf is unaffected — only the calibration number is in question. If you need an accurate figure today
, set `cnyPerCredit` yourself in `cordis.patch.yml`, or close the WorkBuddy app and run `tools/measu
re-rate.mjs` on a clean window.
Put both purses on one line in the DeepSeek Harness sidebar — and convert between them:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Hover for the full breakdown: the conversion rate, the DeepSeek recharge/bonus split, and what the t
full breakdown: the conversion rate, the DeepSeek recharge/bonus split, and what the two add up to.
## Why
In DSH you typically run two balances side by side:
- **WorkBuddy / CodeBuddy credits** — spent through the desktop app's own pool (via `dsh-connect-wor

kbuddy`)
- **DeepSeek official balance** — billed per token in CNY
The two are in different units, so putting them next to each other answers nothing. To know whether
your credit pile is worth more than your wallet — or what both together are worth — the credits have
to be priced in yuan first.
Existing plugins show either raw credits or a CNY balance. None of them do the conversion.
## How the rate is derived (not guessed)
**Step 1 — measure what the credits bought.** Read the tokens every `workbuddy` turn actually consum
ed from DSH's own session logs (`inputTokens` / `cacheReadTokens` / `outputTokens`), and read the cr
edit balance before and after the measurement window.
**Step 2 — price those same tokens at DeepSeek's official rate.** DeepSeek publishes CNY prices per
1M tokens for `deepseek-flash`:
| | Cache hit | Cache miss | Output |
Divide what those tokens would have cost on DeepSeek by the credits they actually consumed.
**Measured on the author's machine:**
| Window | ¥ per credit |

| Off-peak | 0.0295 |
| Peak | 0.0590 |
| **Midpoint (default)** | **0.0440** |
**Cross-check against list price.** WorkBuddy Pro's add-on pack is US$15 / 500 credits = US$0.03/cre
dit. The domestic product bills in CNY, which reads as ¥0.03/credit — the same order of magnitude as
the measured value. Both numbers live in the tooltip so you can compare them.
> Why not just use list price: list price is what you pay to *buy* credits, while the measured value
is what the *work* those credits bought would cost on DeepSeek. They answer different questions, an
d the former moves with promotions. The measured value is the default; both are configurable.
## Install
Requires DSH `0.2.x` and a working `dsh-connect-workbuddy` install (for the credit half).
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then **restart DSH** — bundles load at launch.
### Desktop profile caveat
The `desktop` profile is owned by the Electron app: the CLI writes the dependency, but only a restar
t confirms the bundle actually composed. If the line does not appear, check that `dsh-workbuddy-cny`
is in the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` and that the entry did not fail config validation (activa
tion errors only reach stderr, never the UI).

## Re-calibrate after a price change
`tools/measure-rate.mjs` reproduces the measurement:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
It prints the token totals, what those tokens cost on DeepSeek at both windows, and the implied ¥/cr
edit. Session logs live under `~/.dsh/sessions/<workspace>/session-<id>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd`.
## Where the data comes from
| Data | Source |
| WorkBuddy credits | `dsh-connect-workbuddy`'s same-origin route `/plugins/dsh-connect-workbuddy/us

age` |
| DeepSeek balance | `ctx.deepseekAccount.getBalance()` — the same endpoint the account setti

ngs page uses |
| Token counts | Used only to derive the rate; not read at runtime |
The plugin is **read-only**: no check-in, no claiming, no account switching, no credential access. B
oth figures are a snapshot of the same instant, and a failed read renders as `—`, never as `0`.
## Known limits
- **Needs `dsh-connect-workbuddy`** — without it the WorkBuddy half shows `—` and the DeepSeek half

still works.
- **DeepSeek not signed in** — wallet shows `—`, not ¥0.00.
- **Rate is not live** — re

-run the measurement after upstream price changes.
- Refreshes once a minute, matching the account p
